title: The category $\mathcal C_\infty$ of a directed pseudofunctor and its comparison functor
statement:
Let $I$ be a directed preordered set and $(T_{ij},\Phi_i,\theta_{ij})$ a cocone of categories with
vertex $\mathcal D$ ([det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-cocone]). Assume it is *coherent*: there
are natural isomorphisms $\tau_{ijk}\colon T_{jk}\circ T_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{ik}$ for
$i\le j\le k$ such that

- (normalization) $T_{ii}=\mathrm{Id}$, $\theta_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, and $\tau_{iij}$, $\tau_{ijj}$ are identities;
- (cocycle) for $i\le j\le k\le l$, $\tau_{ikl}\circ T_{kl}(\tau_{ijk})=\tau_{ijl}\circ(\tau_{jkl})_{T_{ij}}$ as maps $T_{kl}T_{jk}T_{ij}\to T_{il}$;
- (compatibility) for $i\le j\le k$, $\theta_{ik}=\theta_{ij}\circ(\theta_{jk})_{T_{ij}}\circ\Phi_k(\tau_{ijk})^{-1}$ as maps $\Phi_kT_{ik}\to\Phi_i$.

Define the category $\mathcal C_\infty$:

- objects are pairs $(i,x)$ with $i\in I$ and $x\in\mathcal C_i$;
- for objects $(i,x)$, $(j,y)$ and $k\ge i,j$ put $H_k:=\Hom_{\mathcal C_k}(T_{ik}x,T_{jk}y)$, and
  for $k\le k'$ let $t_{kk'}\colon H_k\to H_{k'}$ be
  $t_{kk'}(g):=\tau_{jkk',y}\circ T_{kk'}(g)\circ\tau_{ikk',x}^{-1}$. Then
  $$
  \Hom_{\mathcal C_\infty}\bigl((i,x),(j,y)\bigr):=\colim_{k\ge i,j}H_k ,
  $$
  a filtered colimit of sets; write $[k,g]$ for the class of $g\in H_k$;
- the composite of $[k,g]\colon(i,x)\to(j,y)$ and $[k',h]\colon(j,y)\to(l,z)$ is
  $[m,\,t_{k'm}(h)\circ t_{km}(g)]$ for any $m\ge k,k'$, and the identity of $(i,x)$ is $[i,\mathrm{id}_x]$.

The *comparison functor* $\Phi\colon\mathcal C_\infty\to\mathcal D$ is
$\Phi(i,x):=\Phi_i(x)$ and $\Phi([k,g]):=\theta_{jk,y}\circ\Phi_k(g)\circ\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}$.
These are well defined, $\mathcal C_\infty$ is a category and $\Phi$ is a functor.

proof.text:
For fixed $a=(i,x)$ and $b=(j,y)$ write $J_{ab}=\{k\in I:i\le k,\ j\le k\}$. This is a set, is nonempty by directedness, and any two of its elements have an upper bound still in $J_{ab}$. Its category has at most one arrow between any two objects, so parallel arrows are already equal. Thus it is a small filtered category. For $k\le n\le p$, put $A_{a;k,n}=\tau_{ikn,x}$ and $A_{b;k,n}=\tau_{jkn,y}$. The cocycle axiom says
$$A_{b;n,p}T_{np}(A_{b;k,n})=A_{b;k,p}\tau_{knp,T_{jk}y},$$
with the analogous identity for $a$. Consequently
$$t_{np}(t_{kn}(g))=A_{b;k,p}\tau_{knp,T_{jk}y}\,T_{np}T_{kn}(g)\,\tau_{knp,T_{ik}x}^{-1}A_{a;k,p}^{-1}=A_{b;k,p}T_{kp}(g)A_{a;k,p}^{-1}=t_{kp}(g),$$
where the middle equality is naturality of $\tau_{knp}$. Normalization gives $t_{kk}(g)=g$. Hence the displayed Hom sets and transition maps form a diagram of sets indexed by $J_{ab}$.

source.place: The colimit is filtered: index category and transition laws

proof.text: The set colimit can be constructed as the quotient of $\coprod_{k\in J_{ab}}H_k$ by eventual equality: $(k,g)\sim(n,h)$ if there is $p\ge k,n$ with $t_{kp}(g)=t_{np}(h)$. Reflexivity uses $p=k$, symmetry reverses the equality, and transitivity follows by moving two equality witnesses to one upper bound and using the transition law in step 1. The coprojections are compatible, and any compatible family $u_k:H_k\to S$ factors uniquely by $[k,g]\mapsto u_k(g)$, since eventual equality implies equality of these values. This is exactly the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In any chosen colimit, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] gives representatives $[k,g]$ and the same common-stage equality criterion. This justifies the Hom-set construction without assuming existence of any colimit over a large category.

source.place: The colimit is filtered: set colimit and equality of classes; Stacks Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits

proof.text:
For three fixed objects $a=(i,x)$, $b=(j,y)$, $c=(l,z)$ and a stage $m$ above all three indices, write $g_m:T_{im}x\to T_{jm}y$ and $h_m:T_{jm}y\to T_{lm}z$. For $m\le p$, direct cancellation of the middle isomorphisms gives
$$t^{ac}_{mp}(h_mg_m)=\tau_{lmp,z}T_{mp}(h_mg_m)\tau_{imp,x}^{-1}=\bigl(\tau_{lmp,z}T_{mp}(h_m)\tau_{jmp,y}^{-1}\bigr)\bigl(\tau_{jmp,y}T_{mp}(g_m)\tau_{imp,x}^{-1}\bigr)=t^{bc}_{mp}(h_m)t^{ab}_{mp}(g_m).$$
Here the superscripts specify the pair of objects determining $t$. Likewise $t^{aa}_{mp}(\mathrm{id}_{T_{im}x})=\mathrm{id}_{T_{ip}x}$, because a functor preserves identities and conjugating an identity by an isomorphism gives an identity.

source.place: Composition: transition maps preserve composable products and identities

proof.text: Define the composite by the formula in the statement. If $m$ and $n$ are two upper bounds of the representative stages $k,k'$, choose $p\ge m,n$. By steps 1 and 3 the images in stage $p$ of both proposed composite representatives are exactly $t_{k'p}(h)t_{kp}(g)$, so their classes agree. If $[k,g]=[r,\widetilde g]$ and $[k',h]=[s,\widetilde h]$, the equality criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] gives witnesses $u\ge k,r$ and $v\ge k',s$. Choose $p$ above $u,v$ and the two stages used to form the proposed composites. At $p$ the two representatives of each input agree by step 1. Their products therefore agree, by step 3, proving independence of representatives and of the common stage simultaneously.

source.place: Composition: independence of the common stage and representatives

proof.text: For three composable classes choose one stage above their three representative stages. By step 4 both bracketings of their composite are represented there by the two bracketings of the same three morphisms in that stage category, and are equal by its associativity. For $a=(i,x)$, normalization $T_{ii}=\mathrm{Id}$ makes $[i,\mathrm{id}_x]$ a morphism $a\to a$; at every later stage $m$ it is represented by $\tau_{iim,x}T_{im}(\mathrm{id}_x)\tau_{iim,x}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{T_{im}x}$. Thus left and right composition with it reduce to the identity laws at a common stage. The pair objects, Hom sets, composition, and identities now define an ordinary category.

For a representative $g\in H_k$ the map $P_k(g)=\theta_{jk,y}\Phi_k(g)\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}$ has source $\Phi_i(x)$ and target $\Phi_j(y)$ by [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-cocone]. For $k\le n$, cocone compatibility, applied to $i\le k\le n$ and $j\le k\le n$, gives
$$\theta_{in,x}^{-1}=\Phi_n(\tau_{ikn,x})\theta_{kn,T_{ik}x}^{-1}\theta_{ik,x}^{-1},\qquad
\theta_{jn,y}=\theta_{jk,y}\theta_{kn,T_{jk}y}\Phi_n(\tau_{jkn,y})^{-1}.$$
Substitute these and $t_{kn}(g)=\tau_{jkn,y}T_{kn}(g)\tau_{ikn,x}^{-1}$. The two pairs of inverse $\Phi_n(\tau)$ factors cancel, and naturality of the cocone isomorphism $\theta_{kn}:\Phi_nT_{kn}\Rightarrow\Phi_k$ gives
$$P_n(t_{kn}(g))=\theta_{jk,y}\theta_{kn,T_{jk}y}\Phi_nT_{kn}(g)\theta_{kn,T_{ik}x}^{-1}\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}=\theta_{jk,y}\Phi_k(g)\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}=P_k(g).$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], equal classes have representatives equal at a common stage; the displayed invariance therefore makes $\Phi([k,g])=P_k(g)$ independent of representatives.

source.place: The comparison functor: types, compatibility, naturality and descent to classes

proof.text:
Set $\Phi(i,x)=\Phi_i(x)$ on objects. Normalization and functoriality of $\Phi_i$ give $\Phi([i,\mathrm{id}_x])=\theta_{ii,x}\Phi_i(\mathrm{id}_x)\theta_{ii,x}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{\Phi_i(x)}$. For a composable pair use step 4 to represent both morphisms at one stage $m$, say $g_m:T_{im}x\to T_{jm}y$ and $h_m:T_{jm}y\to T_{lm}z$. Step 6 allows their images to be computed at $m$, and
$$\Phi([m,h_m])\Phi([m,g_m])=\theta_{lm,z}\Phi_m(h_m)\theta_{jm,y}^{-1}\theta_{jm,y}\Phi_m(g_m)\theta_{im,x}^{-1}=\theta_{lm,z}\Phi_m(h_mg_m)\theta_{im,x}^{-1}=\Phi([m,h_mg_m]).$$
This proves that the comparison assignment is a functor.

source.place: The comparison functor: preservation of identities and composition
